This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 21.12.2017 in MACC No.20/2015 by Additional MACT, Sardarpur,
district Dhar for enhancement of Rs.2 lakhs as compensation.

2. Facts in brief are that appellant/claimant filed an application under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs for the permanent physical disability caused due to motor vehicle accident dated 25.04.2014 at 9 a.m within the jurisdiction of police station Sardarpur, district Dhar regarding which crime no.182/14 was registered against the driver of Ekta bus No.MP-13-P-1319 being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured by respondent no.3 on the ground that at the time of accident claimant was aged 20 years and was working in the bus as cleaner and earning Rs.9,000/- per month.

The claim was contested by respondent no.3 on the ground of breach of policy conditions including the quantum.

Trial court framed issues, recorded evidence and awarded a total compensation of Rs.63,684/- in the following heads:
 Attendant and special diet Rs.15,0  Loss of income during treatment Rs.17,4  Pain & suffering Rs.30,0
Medical expenses Rs.1224
Total Rs.63,6

sentences.text: 1 4. This appeal has been preferred on the ground that the tribunal committed error in rejecting the claim of permanent physical disability and also committed error in assessing the income on the lower side.
Tribunal also committed error in awarding meager amount in all heads.

5. Heard.
6.
Counsel for the respondent no.3 opposed the appeal and submitted that tribunal has recorded the findings based on evidence.
No enhancement is required.

7. Perused the record.
8.
Tribunal has recorded the finding in para-13 that the injuries in the left leg of the appellant does not affect his earning capacity.
For the correctness of this finding the evidence of appellant and Dr.Devendra Mandloi (PW/2) is being reappreciated.
Dr.Devendra Mandloi (PW/2) has certified 31% permanent disability to the appellant through certificate Ex.P/58.

The basis of this permanent physical disability is the impairment of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:29137 3 MA-2416-2018 moveability of the appellant due to fracture in femur bone, that has caused impairment in movement and sitting.
The claimant/appellant (PW/1) mentions that his foot and teeth were broken and Ex.P/44 mentions that four teethes were missing.
He stated that at the time of accident, he was working as cleaner in Ekta bus and now he is unable to perform his job as cleaner.

The finding of the trial court that earning capacity is not affected due to injuries is recorded without considering the nature of job of the appellant which required physical job along with swift movement.
Accordingly, 10% loss of earning capacity is determined.

On the date of accident i.e.
25.04.2014 the minimum wages payable to an unskilled labourer was Rs.5845/- per month and tribunal also assessed Rs.5820/- per month.
There is only a slight difference between the income assessed by the tribunal and the minimum wages payable to an unskilled labourer.
Applying the multiplier of 18 and adding 40% future prospects the total loss of future income comes to Rs.1,76,753/-.
Accordingly, an amount of Rs.1,76,753/- is awarded in the head of loss of future income.
No amount in the head of transport expenses has been awarded to the appellant by the tribunal.
Considering the treatment in different hospitals an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded in the head of transportation.
The amount in the head of pain and suffering is not awarded adequately

,
therefore, it is enhanced from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.43,247/-.

Thus, the total compensation is recalculated as under:
 Loss of future income Rs.1,76,75  Attendant and special diet Rs.15,000/
 Loss of income during treatment Rs.17,460/
 Transportation Rs.10,000/

9.
Thus, the total compensation in the instant case is Rs.2,63,684/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.63,684/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,00,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
10. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of application till realization.
This enhancement shall be satisfied and disbursed as per para-20 of the award.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
11. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
